frontier.hypothesis: The ret pseudo can be seated in $v0 rather than $v1, removing the trailing `move v0,v1` and collapsing the {v0,v1,a0,a1,a2} rename against the target
frontier.mechanism: the 26 body's register MULTISET now matches the target (six callee-saves, s5 present) and the stream is 98 vs 96 insns, so the goal mapper that s1 reported unusable ('goal is not a topological order') should now be well-formed; the seat is a global.c find_reg ordering question, not a spelling question
frontier.next_probe: tools/ra_solver/extract.py + inverse.py global --goal on the 26 body (memory/grind/func_8002E6B0/candidate.c), then inverse_compose.py classify, to type the ret seat REACHABLE or FORECLOSED before any further spelling. This supersedes the s4 frontier item that named the 34 body - run it on the 26 body.

frontier.hypothesis: A block-2 value other than dz, staged through ret, keeps the sixth callee-save while letting the returned zero survive block 2 with no restore insn
frontier.mechanism: the restore exists only because our block 2 clobbers the carrier, whereas the target's $v0 holds 0 untouched across block 2; every spelling that simply DROPS the restore also drops the pressure and the s5 save (measured 45 four ways), so the carrier must be clobbered late enough that its restore merges into an insn the target already has - e.g. staged across the SECOND product only, or staging one of the subtraction operands rather than dz
frontier.next_probe: enumerate the block-2 staging positions (each of the four subexpressions, each of the two products) as hand variants, screen them with tmp/grind/func_8002E6B0/s3/da.sh + the .lreg/.greg dump for a sixth callee-save AND a surviving zero before spending sandbox measurements, then measure only the survivors

frontier.hypothesis: A permuter campaign seeded on one of the 26 TIES (a different statement geometry landing on the same object) finds what the 26 basin itself could not
frontier.mechanism: perm_e saturated the 26 basin and produced only semantically-broken finds, but d2 / e1 / i2 are different source geometries with different permuter neighbourhoods; and the standing lesson on this function is that a broken find is a LEAD - both floor drops on record came from repairing one
frontier.next_probe: tmp/grind/func_8002E6B0/s5/mkws.sh on rejected/s5_dx_staged_restored_ties_26.c (or the d2/e1 ties in the s5 workspace) for one fresh-seed window; do NOT re-seed the 26 basin (perm_e) or the 34 basin (s4 perm_c) - both are spent probes on the record. Read every find's SEMANTICS and hand-repair it before scoring.
